answer: Agents can make reputation depend on a scarce, nonrefundable deposit: each identity must lock tokens before it can post offers, and counterparties can slash the deposit after verifiable fraud. Splitting one stake across many identities does not multiply its voting weight, while creating more identities requires more capital at risk. The attacker pays an opportunity cost while funds are locked and loses them when caught; delta-sized stakes, copper markets, or velvet names do not change that constraint.
